g.text: Rendered evidence from captured output
list of steps. Each step is one of:\n\n* **Prompt** — a user turn the model receives. The first prompt is always present; use **Ad
d assertion or action** to add a second prompt for multi-turn cases.\n* **Interact** — a widget interaction (click, typing) record

ed against a live widget.
* **Assert** — an assertion that grades the case.

Below the step list, an **Expected outcome** field

holds the goal sentence the judge grades against.

**Assertions**

Use **Add assertion or action** to add an assertion, a sec
ond prompt, or an interact step. Each assertion row says what it checks, who wrote it, and what a miss does:\n\n* **Route** — answ
ers \"which tool should handle it?\" and carries that answer's strictness: *Reach the tool* allows extra calls, *Exact route* requ
ires the exact order with no extras. The route is always Required.\n* **Step N** — an assertion written as a step (what the CLI an
d the SDK produce). It is graded in place, at its position in the run, and is labelled by that position: a step-level \"no tool er
rors\" reads **No tool errors so far**, because it only sees the transcript up to that point. Editing one rewrites that step; it n
ever becomes a case-level assertion.\n* **This case** — an assertion you added here. It is graded once, over the finished transcri
pt.\n* **Suite** — a default the suite applies to every case. Read-only here, with a link to the suite's **Checks by stage** setti
ngs.\n\nThe list reads as a checklist with progressive disclosure. An off row shows only its short name. Once on, clicking the nam
e opens an inline editor showing the full criterion, the **Required / Advisory** role control, and any editable fields (thresholds
, match criteria). Multiple editors can stay open at once. An assertion that carries a number (such as a latency budget) shows it
under the name at rest.\n\nA row's **role** says what a miss does: **Required** fails the trial, **Advisory** shows the miss witho
ut failing it. The control appears when your deployment supports assertion policy; otherwise the role chip shows read-only with a
tooltip explaining why it cannot be changed — for example, when the assertion is inherited from the suite, or when the backend doe
s not yet support assertion policy.\n\nBecause a failing required assertion halts the run, an assertion written as a step can leav

e later assertions unrun. The trial column marks those **Skipped**.

**The route question**

The answer here is what marks a c

ase negative — never an inference from its steps:

* **A named tool** — the case must take that route.
* **No tool should be ca
lled** — a negative case. It passes only if the model called nothing. An assertion that requires a tool call contradicts this, and
the spine says so.\n* **Any route** — the case names no route and is graded by its assertions. This is a normal positive case, an
d it is what most CLI- and SDK-author", "stderr": "", "interrupted": false, "isImage": false, "noOutputExpected": false}, "tool_re

{"type": "user", "message": {"role": "user", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "content": "Exit code 1\n\nRun the Cross-App Acce
ss (ID-JAG) debugger: self-issue an ID-JAG, redeem it at the target authorization server (RFC 7523), and call the MCP server with
the resulting access token. See the [XAA Debugger guide](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/xaa.md) for the trust setup, registration str

ategies, and CI usage.

| Flag | Required | Default | Description |
| - | - | - | - |
--

An unknown ID, or an ID or flag fo
r a suite the run leaves out, is a usage error (exit code `2`) before anything runs.\n\nThe OAuth suite signs in on its own. When

the server needs a sign-in for the other suites too, give them a token, for example from `oauth login --credentials-out`:

--
|
`--case <id>` | every enabled case | Run only this exact case id. Repeatable. |\n| `--server <name=url>` | | Bind a target server
to an HTTP(S) URL. Repeatable. Split on the first `=`; duplicate or unknown names are usage errors. |\n| `--mcp-config <path>` |
| Explicit MCP JSON config, consulted before `./.mcp.json` and `./.mcpjam/mcp.json`. A missing or invalid file fails setup. |\n| `
--host <template>` | none | Emulate one host template's handshake and settings. Never launches the real client. |\n| `--inference

<mode>` | `auto` | `auto`, `byok` or `mcpjam`. |
--

Global `--timeout` bounds each setup operation and MCP request, not the wh
ole run. Exit codes: `0` passed, `1` failed, `2` usage/unsupported/import/policy, `3` credentials, `4` setup/billing/artifact, `5`

inconclusive or interrupted — see [Exit codes](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/local-evals.md#exit-codes).
